tags: why does my dog stretch when i get home
script: You walk through the door and instead of jumping, your dog does a slow, deep stretch, front legs out, rear in the air. It's one of the most charming greetings in the dog world. There are a few reasons behind it. Dogs spend a lot of time resting while you're away, so a stretch simply loosens muscles that are stiff from lying down, just like we stretch after waking up. But it can also be a social signal. The front-down stretch looks a lot like the play bow, which dogs use to say they're friendly and relaxed, so when your dog does it as you arrive, they're welcoming you in a calm, happy way. Some dogs stretch to release the excitement of seeing you, using the movement to settle themselves before the real celebration begins. Stretching is generally healthy, and it's a good sign that your dog feels safe and comfortable around you. If your dog stretches constantly, seems stiff or unwilling to move, or whines while stretching, mention it to your vet, since pain can sometimes look like this. Otherwise, enjoy it as one of the nicest welcome-home rituals.
